sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Pettis County
sections.html:
Deeds for Pettis County land are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office inside the courthouse, 415 South Ohio Ave, Suite 106, Sedalia, MO 65301. Call 660-826-5000 and ask for extension 922. The fax is 660-829-4479 and the email is recorder@pettiscomo.com. Phone the extension for counter hours before you make the drive.

The office records deeds of trust, real estate deeds, releases, easements, subdivision plats, surveys, military discharges, powers of attorney, tax liens and real estate UCC filings. It also issues marriage licenses.

The county's posted schedule shows $24 for page one of a standard document and $3 for each page after it. A $2.00 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 may change the posted figure, so call 660-826-5000 ext 922 for the amount that applies to your paper.

Under county policy the recorder keeps an overpayment of up to $10, which prevents a rejection when a check is a dollar or two off. To have an overpayment returned, ask in writing within thirty days of the recording date, and the recorder then has thirty days to answer.

sections.h2: Can I search Pettis County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The recorder's page offers several routes, each covering a different span of years:

  • Land records from 1983 to the present through the Fidlar Tapestry portal, which also holds marriage license and plat or survey searches back to 1833
  • A free online index book for land records research from 1833 through 1994, hosted at recordhub.cottsystems.com
  • Laredo, a monthly subscription with round the clock remote access to current data and images
  • Tapestry, a pay as you go service for people who search only now and then

Certified and plain copies of marriage licenses can be ordered through Official Records Online. If a house has been in a family since before 1983, check the older index book first, because the later database starts that year.

sections.h2: What the recorder can and cannot look up
sections.html:
The county FAQ sets clear limits. Staff cannot search by street address, so you need a legal description, a book and page, an owner name, the year of recording or a document number. People who have only an address are sent to the assessor's office in Suite 218.

The recorder is barred from running lien searches, since liens can also be filed with other offices, though staff will help you search the indexes yourself. A recorded deed does not have to state the sale price, so the office cannot tell you what a neighbor's house sold for. For easements, check the original plat and the indexes, because there is no separate easement index.

Changing a name on a deed takes a new document, and the office does not prepare it. A title company or attorney does that work. After recording, expect the original back within about two weeks.

Pettis County follows the state layout statute, RSMo 59.310, which lets a recorder refuse a paper that falls short. The county fee schedule adds a $25 nonstandard charge for papers accepted despite format problems and points to the Recorders Association website for the formatting standards.

The statute calls for printing on one side, in dark ink, with type of at least eight point, on light colored stock of twenty pound weight or heavier. Keep the top three inches of page one empty for the recorder's certificate, and put a typed or printed name under each signature. Draft the deed with those points in mind, since a rejected paper means another trip or another mailing.

This is a free notification service for property owners, described on the county page as protection against property fraud, which happens when someone uses your property for financial gain. The recorder runs a similar sign-up for notaries called Notary Fraud Alert. Both links sit on the recorder's page and run through Fidlar.

If you inherit a Pettis County house or rent one out from a distance, an alert costs nothing and sets up monitoring for the address.

sections.h2: Marriage licenses, copies and other filings
sections.html:
A marriage license costs $60 including one certified copy, with extra copies at $1 plain or $9 certified. Plain copies of recorded documents are $1 a page, and certifying a document is another $1. Survey pages are $24 for the first and $5 for each one after.

UCC fixture filings on the approved form with the required addendum are priced like a standard document, $24 for page one and $3 for each additional page. The office also records military discharges and tax liens.

sections.h2: Pettis County at a glance for sellers
sections.html: Pettis County covers about 682 square miles of west central Missouri, and Sedalia is both the seat and the largest city. The July 2025 population estimate is 44,254, up from 42,980 in 2020. Owners occupy 69.1 percent of households, the typical home is valued at $166,300, median gross rent is $885 and median household income is $60,430.

sections.h2: Steps from signing to recorded deed
sections.html:
1. Have a title company or attorney prepare the deed, since the recorder's office does not draft documents.
  2. Check page one for the three empty inches at the top, dark type of at least eight point, and a printed name under each signature.
  3. Look up the current fee at ext 922, and write one check that covers it. Because the office keeps up to $10 of an overpayment, a small cushion avoids a rejection.
  4. Bring or mail the paper to Suite 106, or let the closing agent deliver it for you.
  5. Expect the original to come back within about two weeks, and keep it with your closing papers.

Anything that fails the format test can still be recorded for the $25 nonstandard charge, but fixing it before you submit saves money and a second trip.

sections.h2: Who to call before a sale
sections.html:
The assessor, collector and recorder all work in the courthouse at 415 S Ohio, so a title check takes one stop.

  • Assessor, Suite 218, ext 920, for the parcel's classification and value
  • Collector, Suite 216, ext 921, for tax statements and paid receipts
  • Recorder, Suite 106, ext 922, for recorded deeds and releases

Ask the collector for the current year's balance before closing day, and allow time for any payment to post. In a cash sale the same offices apply, and the buyer's title company handles the recording once the deed is signed.

faqs.q: Is the posted recorder fee schedule current?
faqs.a: The posted schedule shows $24 for page one. A $2.00 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 may apply, so call 660-826-5000 ext 922 for the amount charged today.

faqs.q: Can staff find a deed if I only know the street address?
faqs.a: No. The recorder needs a legal description, a book and page, a name, the recording year or a document number. The assessor's office can supply the legal description from the address.

faqs.q: How long until I get my original deed back?
faqs.a: The county FAQ says you should receive the original within two weeks of recording.

faqs.q: Does a Pettis County deed show the sale price?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The selling price is not required on a recorded deed, so the recorder cannot report what a nearby home sold for.

faqs.q: What if I overpay the recording fee?
faqs.a: The recorder keeps overpayments of up to $10 under county policy. To get a refund, send a written request within thirty days of the recording date.
